5504:
** χθές**,
_adverb_ (_lengthened_ **ἐχθές** (which see); where the word occurs in **NT,** {{NT|NT.John.4.52, NT.Act.7.28, NT.Heb.13.8, codices vary between ἐχθές}} and χθέ; χθές is not found in Ptolemaic papyri, but in {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|“PLond.” 2.161.8 (3rd c.AD))}}:—**yesterday,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|hymnus ad Mercurium 273, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.113, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 327a, “Smp.” 174a, etc.: frequently placed between _Article_ and}} _substantive_, ἡ χ. ὁμολογία, οἱ χ. λόγοι,{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 216a, “Ti.” 26e; τῇ χ. ἡμέρᾳ 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.773e}}; χ. μὲν.., τὰ νῦν δὲ.. [{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 17a: frequently πρώην τε καὶ χ., χ. καὶ πρώην, see at {πρώην} 11}}]; χ. καὶ τρίτην ἡμέραν variant in {{LXX+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.3.11, cf. LXX.Gen.31.2}}. (Cf. Sanskrit _hyás_ 'yesterday', Latin _heri, hesternus,_ OHG. **gestaron** 'yesterday', etc.)

5577:
** ψευδομαρτῠρ-ία**, ἡ,
**false witness,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 41.16 codices; ψευδομαρτυρίαν καταγνῶναί τινος 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 12.6 codices: ἐν ψευδομαρτυρίαις 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.53}} codices: but mostly in _genitive_ _plural_, ψευδομαρτυριῶν διάκρισις {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 937b; -ιῶν δίκη 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 3.6; κρίσεις 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1263b21}}; -ιῶν ἑλεῖν τινα to convict, and ἁλῶναι to be convicted, of **perjury,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 5.15, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.7, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.25, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.85; ὀφλεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.74}}; -ιῶν ἐπισκήψασθαί τινι make allegation of **perjury** against one, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.7}}; etc. (This form is perhaps always corrupt in codices of classical authors; -ίων (_genitive_ _plural_ _neuter_, compare {ψευδομαρτυρίου}) should probably be read for -ιῶν, and may be restored for -ίαν in {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 41.16, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 12.6}}; so -ίοις for -ίαις in {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.53: των ψευδομαρτυριων}} is unaccented in Papyrus of {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “adv. Philippum” 12: ψευδομαρτυρια[ν}} is an uncertain restoration in {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“IG” 5(2).357.3 (Stymphalus, 3rd c.BC)}}; but the _feminine_ form existed later, {{NT|NT.Matt.15.19, 26.59.)}}

5598:
** Ω**, ὦ, τό,
twenty-fourth and last letter of the Ionic alphabet, ἀπὸ ἄλφα ἕως.ω. {{Refs 9th c.AD+|“Corpus Glossariorum Latinorum” iii 283 (9th c.AD)}}; thence used as a symbol of **the end, the last,** ἐγώ εἰμι τὸ ἄλφα καὶ τὸ ὦ (not τὸ ὦ μέγα) {{NT|NT.Rev.1.8, +others}}:—as a numeral ώ = 800, but ωνυμ = 800, 000. The epichoric _Attic dialect_ and other alphabets of the Inscrr. had used o in differently to represent the sounds of the later ο and ω: Ω is a differentiated form of ο, and, though usually = ω, was used in the Ionic islands of Paros, Thasos, and Siphnos with the value ο, while O or O represented the sound ω. The name of the letter was τὸ ὦ (_perispomenon_ _accusative_ to {{Refs 5th c.BC+|2nd c.AD(?): Helladius Epigrammaticus cited in Phot. p.530B.), compare 5th c.BC: Achaeus Tragicus 33.3, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 244d, “Cra.” 420b, “Tht.” 203c}}: after the loss of the distinction between long and short vowels, ο and ω had the same pronunciation; they begin to be confused in Papyri of {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC}}(οἰκωνόμου {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“PRev.Laws” 50.22 (3rd c.BC))}}, but the name ω μέγα appears first in later Greek, {{Refs 9th c.AD+|9th c.AD: Theognostus Grammaticus “Can.” 13; κατὰ σχῆμα διπλοῦ ω ¯ ἤτοι μεγάλου 12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 869.26; οἱ δὲ περὶ Ἀρίσταρχον αὐτὸ τὸ ποτήριον ω ¯ μέγα εἶναί φασιν, ὁποῖν ἴσως τὸ κατὰ δύο ῡ ἐσχηματισμένον [prev. author] 869.29}}; ἐν τῷ ω ¯ μεγάλῳ under **omega** (in a lexicon), {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|[prev. author] 1828.49: διὰ τοῠ ω ¯ μεγάλου 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus “Epim.” 208.}}
